en.question: A quote-drafting assistant produces parseable JSON with numeric prices and discounts. Some drafts nevertheless combine discounts in ways forbidden by the company's authoritative pricing rules. A separate content screen already checks abusive language. What should be added before a quote is published?

options.text: A second JSON parser that rejects nonnumeric prices and confirms all required quote fields are present.
options.note: Parsing and field presence do not evaluate relationships between valid numeric values. The reported failures already pass those structural checks.

options.text: An additional model-based content screen trained to classify whether a quote appears commercially reasonable.
options.note: A reasonableness classifier is not the authoritative discount calculation. The policy defines exact business rules that can be checked directly rather than inferred from appearance.

options.text: Recalculate allowed discounts and block quotes that fail the authoritative pricing rules before publication.
options.note: The pricing rules provide a precise application-level invariant independent of fluent output or valid JSON. Checking before publication prevents an invalid quote from becoming a customer commitment.

options.text: A post-publication reconciliation job that flags inconsistent discounts for the sales team to amend.
options.note: Reconciliation can detect an incident but permits a forbidden quote to be published first. It does not meet the requested pre-publication control requirement.
